## Detailed entries

### Adair County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** 2026-03-18, per signed Adair County Board of Supervisors minutes: Resolution #2026-26 adopted by unanimous 5-0 roll call (Hoadley, Baier, Wedemeyer, Christoffersen, Walker all aye).
- **Date field:** `2026-03-18` (exact)
- **Duration:** Until the Board imposes a permanent moratorium by resolution, passes an ordinance regulating the structures, or rescinds the temporary moratorium; no calendar end date (Resolution #2026-26).
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, battery storage
- **Record ID:** `ia-adair-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Resolution #2026-26, "Resolution to Establish a Temporary Moratorium on the Construction of Data Centers, High-Density Computing Facilities, and Battery Storage Facilities in the Unincorporated Areas of Adair County, Iowa," adopted March 18, 2026 by unanimous 5-0 roll call.
- **What prompted it:** Proposed 765 kV MISO transmission line, land negotiations in the Hebron area, and concern that data centers require large amounts of electricity and water.
- **Affected projects:** Applied Digital interest in a 200 MW data center near Adair reported in Clarke County coverage; no Adair County project approval record captured.
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-09-23. On Sept. 9, 2026 the Board repealed and rescinded Resolution No. 2026-45 (the Adair County Data Center Regulatory Ordinance) because the required public hearing had not yet been held; that did not affect the Resolution #2026-26 moratorium. A public hearing on the data center regulatory ordinance was set for 9:15 a.m. on 2026-09-23; its outcome was not yet reported at research time. The Board also set a $500 data center permit fee in August 2026.
- **Outcome:** Supervisors continued reviewing a draft data center ordinance after adoption of the moratorium. The draft would require data-center equipment to be housed in permanent structures on foundations, not shipping containers or similar temporary structures (March 25, 2026 Western Iowa Today: "No action was taken on the ordinance today" — confirms ordinance was still in draft a week after the moratorium passed).

### Audubon County

- **What prompted it:** County has no specific ordinance for utility-scale BESS; time needed to coordinate with agencies and create ordinances.
- **Affected projects:** One company considering a BESS in the county reportedly supported the pause.
- **Status notes:** Recorded extended following the May 5, 2026 adoption of Resolution 2026-25 through May 1, 2027 or earlier permanent BESS development ordinance. Complete later-action history, actual operative interval and current legal force remain unverified.
- **Outcome:** —

- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `ia-woodbury-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Resolution 14064, Twelve (12) month Moratorium on the acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for all classes of data centers within the unincorporated areas of Woodbury County, Iowa.
- **What prompted it:** Regulatory gap on siting and review of data-center applications in unincorporated Woodbury County.
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-07-31.
- **Outcome:** Twelve-month pause on accepting, processing, or approving data-center applications in unincorporated Woodbury County.

### SF657 (2025)

- **Policy ID:** `ia-sf657-2025`
- **Sponsor / party:** Senate Ways and Means Committee; Committee bill
- **Status:** Signed by Governor 2025-06-06, Acts Chapter 136
- **Provisions:** Created the Business Incentives for Growth (BIG) program. The eligibility rules in the new Code section 15.504 require the business to be "primarily engaged in advanced manufacturing, bioscience, insurance and finance, or technology and innovation" and explicitly exclude data center businesses, retail businesses, and certain restricted-membership businesses ("The business shall not be a data center business, a retail business, or a business where a cover charge or membership requirement restricts certain individuals from entering the business"). Data center business is defined by reference to Iowa Code 423.3(95).
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_restriction; fiscal
